universal_lens: The SPORT framework unifies spherical video compression and power optimization via a geometrically consistent truncation operator. By mapping bit-depth reduction directly to Weighted Spherical PSNR (WS-PSNR), it establishes an isomorphism between perceptual quality constraints and memory bandwidth conservation, ensuring optimal resource allocation across non-uniform spatial domains. A unified mathematical framework for 360° video quality assessment integrating WS-PSNR with ERP geometry and truncation consistency.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, gaze-predictive tile classification acts as a conformal Bayesian filter. It dynamically updates the posterior probability of a pixel's relevance based on head-tracking priors, allowing the system to allocate high-resolution inference strictly where the epistemic uncertainty of viewer attention is lowest. Bayesian inference models for gaze-predictive region segmentation using WS-PSNR-weighted error metrics to optimize bit allocation across ERP regions.
gse_mapping: GSE models this as a state-transition engine: the display buffer transitions from a uniform high-energy state to a truncated low-energy state based on real-time foveal tracking. The 9.33 ms latency constraint dictates the temporal horizon for valid predictive state updates in the situational reasoning layer. Situation-aware state transitions in TrunMEM360 architecture dynamically adjust truncation levels based on FoV, border, and background pixel weights.

primitives.name: Spherical-PSNR Optimized Truncation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specifically, a new bit-truncation framework is developed to use weighted-to-spherically-uniform PSNR (WSPSNR) directly in the optimization constraint, eliminating the metric inconsistency that arises when standard PSNR is used for a WS-PSNR quality target.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: WSPSNR: Weighted Spherical Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (dimensionless, dB scale); Standard PSNR: Planar Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (dimensionless, dB scale).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes equirectangular projection distortion can be perfectly compensated by latitude weighting; assumes truncation error behaves additively in the noise domain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down at extreme latitudes near poles where pixel density approaches singularity, or if the dummy pattern fails to maintain integer validity under aggressive bit-shifting.

layer2.mapping: Maps the geometric distortion of spherical projections to a linear algebraic truncation problem, preserving perceptual fidelity while minimizing byte-level storage requirements.
layer2.telemetry: Measured deviation between WSPSNR and SSIM thresholds (e.g., < 0.1 dB).

primitives.name: Latency-Compensated Foveal Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Also, gaze-predictive tile classification compensates for the 9.33 ms end-to-end pipeline latency, reducing boundary misclassifications by 5.2 percentage points at a cost of only 0.01 ms.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Latency: Time delay (ms); Misclassification Rate: Probability of incorrect tile categorization (percentage); Computational Cost: Processing time overhead (ms).
primitives.assumptions: Viewer head motion follows a predictable kinematic trajectory over short temporal windows; computational overhead of prediction is negligible compared to memory access savings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during sudden, erratic head snaps exceeding the predictive model's maximum angular velocity threshold, causing temporary foveal blurring.

layer2.mapping: Derives a temporal lookahead kernel that shifts the active FoV mask forward in time, aligning hardware write operations with future perceptual demands.

primitives.name: Foveal Integrity Preserver
primitives.verbatim_quote: In addition, the developed SPORT-B variant which keeps the FoV lossless achieves 47.9% memory power saving and 47.9% bandwidth reduction across different 4K video sequences while satisfying all three per-region WS-PSNR thresholds and maintaining SSIM = 1.000 in the attended region.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: SSIM: Structural Similarity Index Measure (dimensionless, 0 to 1); Power Saving: Reduction in energy consumption (percentage); Bandwidth Reduction: Decrease in data throughput (percentage).
primitives.assumptions: Human visual acuity drops sharply outside the central fovea, permitting aggressive truncation in peripheral regions without perceived quality loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System saturation if the Field of View expands beyond hardware-defined tile boundaries, forcing fallback to uniform resolution and negating power gains.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a hierarchical attention mechanism in neural networks, where high-fidelity gradients are preserved only at the focal point while peripheral activations are quantized.
layer2.telemetry: Maintenance of SSIM = 1.000 within the tracked FoV.

primitives.name: Motion-to-Photon Safety Margin Enforcer
primitives.verbatim_quote: The total motion-to-photon latency of 9.33 ms satisfies the 20 ms VR comfort budget with a 53.3% safety margin.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Motion-to-Photon Latency: Total system response time (ms); Comfort Budget: Maximum tolerable latency before inducing cybersickness (ms); Safety Margin: Percentage of unused budget.
primitives.assumptions: A fixed 20 ms threshold universally applies to user comfort; system clock jitter does not cause transient spikes above the 9.33 ms mean.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violates comfort constraints if background processes interrupt the display pipeline, pushing latency beyond the 20 ms hard limit.

layer2.mapping: Functions as a strict temporal bound in the GSE state machine, vetoing any rendering path that threatens to exceed the physiological comfort threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Real-time monitoring of end-to-end pipeline latency against the 20 ms cap.

primitives.name: Weighted Structural Similarity PSNR
primitives.verbatim_quote: WSPSNR helps mitigate this problem by weighting the squared error of each pixel accordingly [7]: WS-MSE = PN i=1 wi(Yi -Xi)2 PN i=1 wi , wi = cos(φi), (9) WS-PSNR = 10 log10 2552 WS-MSE.

primitives.assumptions: Pixel-wise error is weighted inversely proportional to surface area of spherical element.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When cos(φi) approaches zero (near poles), weight diminishes, reducing influence of polar errors on overall metric.

layer2.mapping: Enables consistent quality evaluation across 360° video by correcting for uneven pixel density in ERP projections.

primitives.name: TrunMEM360 Latency Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Because TrunMEM360 completes its write in 2.15 ms while the GPU render takes 3.32 ms, TrunMEM360 adds zero net latency to the critical path.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When T_write > T_gpu, pipeline stalls; otherwise, no additional delay occurs.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational doctrine of the SPORT primitive rests on the rejection of uniform resource allocation in non-Euclidean visual spaces. Traditional video pipelines treat every pixel as equally valuable, a flat-earth assumption that collapses under the geometry of 360-degree immersion. By introducing the Weighted Spherical PSNR (WS-PSNR) directly into the bit-truncation optimization constraint, we establish a rigorous mathematical bridge between perceptual psychology and silicon efficiency. The core derivation relies on the realization that truncating least significant bits (LSBs) in peripheral vision introduces noise that is mathematically invisible to the human observer, yet yields massive reductions in memory bandwidth. This is not merely compression; it is a dynamic reallocation of thermodynamic cost. The gaze-predictive classifier further refines this by anticipating the user's trajectory, effectively solving a differential equation of attention over a 9.33 ms horizon. The resulting system operates as a closed-loop control mechanism where the 'state' is the visual field and the 'control input' is the bit-depth assigned to each tile. The validation on the TrunMEM360 ASIC proves that this theoretical construct translates flawlessly into physical reality, achieving byte-exact agreement between software simulation and hardware execution. Thus, the primitive transcends simple engineering, offering a sovereign law for efficient information processing in immersive environments.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive descends from the early days of foveated rendering in computer graphics, initially proposed to alleviate GPU load. However, it diverges by targeting the memory subsystem rather than the compute unit. It inherits the mathematical rigor of rate-distortion optimization from classical coding theory but adapts it to the specific curvature of spherical projections. The lineage also connects to neuroscience models of retinal acuity, translating biological efficiency into digital circuit design.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the VR headset not just as a display, but as an agent attempting to predict the user's intent. The system assumes the user is an entity whose attention is highly localized and temporally continuous. By predicting where the user will look next, the system pre-emptively allocates resources, acting as a proactive servant rather than a reactive device. This mirrors how a coach anticipates a player's movement to position support efficiently.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists at the boundary of the Field of View. If the predictive model fails and a high-motion object enters the fovea from a truncated peripheral zone, the system must instantly halt truncation to prevent jarring artifacts. Furthermore, if the motion-to-photon latency spikes due to thermal throttling, the safety margin vanishes, triggering a mandatory fallback to uniform resolution to preserve user comfort, overriding all power-saving directives.

reasoning_traces.think: The derivation begins with the fundamental constraint of memory bandwidth in immersive 360-degree video systems. Traditional compression treats the spherical projection uniformly, ignoring the highly non-uniform resolution of the human visual system. By partitioning the frame into fixed-size tiles (64x64 pixels), we establish a discrete spatial basis. The core innovation lies in the introduction of a gaze-dependent metric tensor that classifies these tiles into FoV, Border, and Background. This classification is not merely semantic but dictates a rigorous mathematical operation: Least Significant Bit (LSB) truncation. For the FoV, the truncation depth \tau is zero, preserving the identity mapping and ensuring lossless quality. As we move peripherally, \tau increases, effectively projecting the high-dimensional RGB vectors onto a coarser lattice. This process is formalized via a C++ host application that orchestrates the extraction of pixel values and their corresponding truncation masks from a CSV dataset. The physical realization relies on an FPGA acting as a temporal bridge, generating precise control signals—Precharge Bar, Wordline Enable, etc.—to synchronize the TrunMEM SRAM operations. The empirical validation, showing negligible differences between software simulation and the fabricated Sky130 ASIC, confirms that this bitwise projection accurately models the trade-off between bandwidth reduction and perceptual fidelity. The underlying epistemic structure reveals that information value is strictly local and dependent on the observer's instantaneous state (gaze).
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to early psychophysical studies on peripheral vision acuity, later formalized in rate-distortion theory for image compression. It evolves through ROI-based coding standards (like H.264/AVC) but diverges by implementing the distortion function directly in silicon memory architecture rather than purely algorithmic post-processing, bridging cognitive science and VLSI design. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the system, the 'opposing agent' is the inherent entropy of high-resolution video data attempting to overwhelm the memory bus. The TrunMEM architecture adopts a predictive stance, modeling the user's gaze trajectory. By anticipating where the user will *not* look, it preemptively discards low-value bits, effectively outmaneuvering bandwidth constraints through cognitive alignment rather than brute-force storage expansion.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto condition arises if the predicted gaze deviates significantly from the actual foveal point due to latency in the eye-tracking subsystem. If the misalignment pushes a high-detail object into the Background region, the aggressive truncation will introduce irreversible artifacts. Furthermore, if the truncation depth \tau approaches the bit-depth limit of the sensor, quantization noise may bleed into adjacent tiles during subsequent filtering, violating the isolation assumption of the tiling operator.
